newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA HIKES INSURANCE FIRMS CAPITAL REQUIREMENT.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA HIKES INSURANCE FIRMS CAPITAL REQUIREMENT.

text.p: Bulgaria's cabinet proposed to increase tenfold the capital requirements for licensing insurance firms in order to provide a stable insurance market, government officials said on Monday.
"The capital raise requirement is related to inflation and changes in the foreign exchange rate," Finance Minister Muravei Radev told reporters.
"It aimes to provide guarantees for the insured and prevents the formation of insurance pyramid schemes," he said.
The proposals have have yet to be passed by parliament as amendments to the insurance law, adopted by parliament nine months ago.
Under the law Bulgarian insurance companies were expected to register in an Insurance Supervision Directorate (ISD), which so far has not been formed.

Under the cabinet's proposal the minimum capital requirement for life insurance companies rises from 200 million levs to two billion levs, for property insurance companies from 300 million levs to three billion levs and reinsurance firms from 400 million levs to 3.5 billion levs.
A grave financial and economic crisis pressed the lev from 230 to the dollar in September 1996 to 1,667 on Monday.
The proposed amendments also ban insurance companies from providing security services, Justice Minister Vassil Gotsev said.
Many security firms, set up by former security services employees are also registered as insurance companies and are involved in racketeering.

The cabinet has also proposed to set up a Unified National Insurance Council which will consist of representatives of judicial, investigation and tax authorities, said Gotsev. The council will have a final say on licensing.
Insurance licences are to be requested in one month after the (ISD) is set up.
Some 100 insurance companies operate in the country now, said Radev, but economists predict that very few will be able to meet the new capital requirements.
"Firms can cover the new capital requirements, through increasing their capital, through merging several companies or setting up joint ventures with foreign insurers," said Radev.
Under the law foreign insurers can participate in the local market only in joint ventures with local insurers.
Those firms which fail to meet the new licensing requirements, will continue to operate until their insurance contracts expire, said Radev. -- Elisaveta Konstantinova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-981-4145
